Repo (git worktree; do not push): C:\Users\cable\Documents\dev\zig-parquet\.claude\worktrees\zig-parquet-perf-compat-dc9ccc. No other agent is active; you may edit zig-parquet/src/core/dynamic_reader.zig, zig-parquet/src/core/column_decoder.zig, zig-parquet/src/tests/*.zig, zig-parquet/bench/main.zig, CHANGELOG.md, AGENTS.md. Stage by file name. Read docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-perf-dual-zig-plan.md lines 54-97 (R2-R4) and `git show f7f5dc4 0ed9219 eb85c6c` first. Toolchains: 0.16 = C:/Users/cable/tools/zig-x86_64-windows-0.16.0/zig.exe ; 0.17 = `zig` with `zig build --cache-dir ../.zig17/cache test ...`. Run from repo root: `make test-lib CODECS=zig-only ZIG=<Z>` (add `--summary all` by running the zig command directly inside a `(cd zig-parquet && ...)` subshell), `make test-cli CODECS=zig-only ZIG=<Z>`, `make wasm ZIG=<Z>`. Expected: 911/911 lib, 32/32 cli on both, plus your new tests. The reviewer's repro assets exist at C:\Users\cable\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-cable-Documents-dev-zig-parquet--claude-worktrees-zig-parquet-perf-compat-dc9ccc\4a418477-b813-4383-add3-4d1bca26fb93\scratchpad\rev\zig-parquet\src\tests\review_test.zig and ...\scratchpad\gen\mk.py (pyarrow generator; `uv run` is available in test-files-arrow/ if you need to regenerate; a committed fixture under test-files-arrow must be produced by generate.py, so prefer a hand-built V2 page in the test, or an in-memory codec mutation as the reviewer did).

FINDINGS TO FIX (reviewer's words, verified by repro):
1. MUST-FIX, dynamic_reader.zig ≈:896 and the V2 page path ≈:1075-1086: when borrowing is on, the chunk is read into the arena only for codec == .uncompressed; otherwise it is a gpa allocation freed by the `defer` at ≈:903. A DataPageV2 with `is_compressed = false` inside a SNAPPY/ZSTD chunk (and the empty-values shortcut at ≈:1082) slices `values_data` from that gpa chunk, so borrowed `bytes_val` slices dangle after return. Real wild files (issue206, issue229, issue276_9_per_page, issue368) hit that branch (dictionary pages, safe today); a PLAIN page there is a use-after-free. Fix: when borrowing, always read the chunk into the arena (`chunk_alloc = page_alloc; free_chunk = free_pages` or equivalent) so every borrowed slice is arena-backed regardless of codec. Add a regression test: build a file with a compressed codec in metadata but a V2 PLAIN string page with is_compressed=false (hand-built, or write normally then mutate `metadata.row_groups[0].columns[0].meta_data.?.codec` in memory as the reviewer did), read via readAllRows, rowIterator and rowIteratorStreaming under std.testing.allocator, and assert values. Make sure the test fails before your fix (run it once on the unfixed code) and passes after.
2. SHOULD-FIX, column_decoder.zig ≈:2330/:2360 and ≈:2309 (FLBA dictionary decode with BIT_PACKED levels): `pos += try rle.bitPackedSize(...)` is never checked against value_data.len before `value_data[pos..]`. Add `if (bytes > value_data.len - pos) return error.EndOfData;` before each `pos +=` (pos <= len invariant: state it in a comment). Add a short malformed-page test.
3. SHOULD-FIX, dynamic_reader.zig ≈:888-890: the threadlocal `borrow_bytes` is set before `readColumnChunkData` does I/O; under an evented std.Io another fiber could run a decoder while it is set. Move the set (and its defer reset) to right after the chunk read so no I/O happens while the flag is on.
4. SHOULD-FIX: (a) `RowIterator` now keeps arena capacity after exhaustion; reset with `.free_all` (or deinit the arena) when `next()` returns null so iterate-to-end-without-deinit leaks nothing as before; (b) document `column_decoder.borrow_bytes` as internal-only in its doc comment (and if `internals` re-exports column_decoder, say in the comment that setting it from outside yields dangling slices).
5. SHOULD-FIX, dynamic_reader.zig ≈:383-390: `StreamingRowIterator.next()` increments `current_rg` before `loadGroup`, so an error skips that row group on retry. Match `RowIterator`: increment only after a successful load (or make the iterator terminal after an error — pick what RowIterator does). Add a test if cheap (an injected failing allocator on loadGroup works: first next() fails with OOM, second next() with a working allocator returns the first group's rows).
6. NIT, bench/main.zig: `readAll` only counts rows; add a cheap checksum of the first column (e.g. wrapping-add of int64 values / byte lengths) compared against a value computed from the generated data, so a decoder returning nulls fails the bench. Keep the timed region the same.
7. NIT: CHANGELOG.md — confirm the Unreleased entry mentions `StreamingRowIterator` / `rowIteratorStreaming()` and its contract; add if missing. AGENTS.md — remove the plan-internal "(task 1.2)" reference.

FINISH: 0.16 `zig fmt` on your files (never 0.17 fmt). Commits: `fix(read): arena-backed chunk whenever bytes are borrowed (V2 uncompressed page in compressed chunk)`, `hardening(read): bounds-check bit-packed level sizes in FLBA dictionary decode`, `fix(read): set borrow flag after I/O; free RowIterator arena on exhaustion; streaming iterator retries a failed group`, `bench: verify a column checksum`, `docs: changelog streaming iterator, AGENTS cleanup` — each ending `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Then run the gate: lib + cli tests on both toolchains with counts, `make wasm` on both, and `make bench ZIG=<Z16>` once to confirm file_MB unchanged and read_stream numbers within noise of (int64_plain ~140M, str_dict ~76M, str_unique ~61M, mixed5 ~21M rows/s). Report: per-finding what you changed, test counts, bench line, commit hashes.

# AGENTS.md

## Project Overview

zig-parquet is a native Parquet library written in Zig 0.16.0. It provides read/write support for Parquet files, a C ABI, and a CLI tool (`pqi`). Read `README.md` for the full feature list and API examples.

## Project Structure

- `zig-parquet/` - Core Parquet library
- `cli/` - `pqi` CLI tool
- `zig-{zstd,brotli,lz4,gzip,snappy}/` - Pure Zig compression codec packages
- `test-files-arrow/` - Test files generated by Python (uses uv)
- `test-files-wild/` - Real-world Parquet files for compatibility testing

### Key Files

- `zig-parquet/src/lib.zig` - Library exports (package root)
- `zig-parquet/src/core/dynamic_reader.zig` - DynamicReader (schema-agnostic row reading)
- `zig-parquet/src/core/column_decoder.zig` - Column value decoding (encodings, levels, types)
- `zig-parquet/src/core/writer.zig` - High-level typed Parquet writer
- `zig-parquet/src/core/dynamic_writer.zig` - DynamicWriter (runtime-schema row writing)
- `zig-parquet/src/core/format.zig` - Parquet format types (re-exports from format/)
- `zig-parquet/src/core/safe.zig` - Safe casting/slicing helpers for untrusted data
- `zig-parquet/src/core/arrow_batch.zig` - Arrow C Data Interface bridge
- `zig-parquet/src/core/schema.zig` - Recursive schema for nested types + logical types
- `cli/src/main.zig` - pqi CLI entry point

### Documentation

- `ROADMAP.md` - Development phases and progress
- `zig-parquet/HARDENING.md` - Hardening guidelines
- `test-files-wild/README.md` - Test file validation status

### References

- Parquet format spec: https://github.com/apache/parquet-format
- Thrift Compact Protocol: https://github.com/apache/thrift/blob/master/doc/specs/thrift-compact-protocol.md

## Build & Test

**Always run from the repo root via `make`. Never `cd` into `zig-parquet/` or `cli/`** — the tool session preserves cwd across commands, so a stray `cd` strands later commands in the wrong directory. The Makefile's recipes handle the `cd` in a subshell so the outer cwd is unchanged.

`test`, `lib`, and `cli` accept `CODECS=<spec>` and `OPT=<ReleaseSmall|ReleaseFast|ReleaseSafe|Debug>` as make variables — don't add new fixed targets for each combination.

```bash
make help                              # List all targets with examples
make build                             # Build library + CLI (defaults)
make test                              # Library tests, all codecs (Zig preferred)
make test CODECS=zig-only              # Pure Zig codecs only (no C deps)
make test CODECS=c-only                # C/C++ codecs only
make test CODECS=none                  # Non-compression tests only
make test CODECS=c-zstd,zstd           # Cross-implementation (both zstd codecs)
make lib CODECS=c-brotli OPT=ReleaseSmall  # Size-measured release build
make example NAME=basic                # Build an example (NAME is required)
make example NAME=wasm_demo OPT=ReleaseSmall
make wasm                              # Verify WASM targets compile and link
make validate-wild                     # Validate pqi against wild files (failures)
make validate-wild-all                 # Validate pqi against wild files (all)
make fmt                               # zig fmt across sources
make clean                             # Remove .zig-cache and zig-out everywhere
```

`CODECS` values: `all` (default), `none`, `zig-only`, `c-only`, or comma-separated list from `zstd,snappy,gzip,lz4,brotli` (Zig) and `c-zstd,c-snappy,c-gzip,c-lz4,c-brotli` (C/C++).

## Zig 0.16.0 — Key API Patterns

Always search the codebase for existing patterns before writing new code.

### std.Io Interface

Zig 0.16 uses a unified `std.Io` interface for all I/O. File operations require an `io: std.Io` parameter.

- **In `main`**: Accept `std.process.Init` — provides `init.io`, `init.gpa`
- **In tests**: Use `std.testing.io`
- **In library code**: Thread `io` through from caller

### File I/O

```zig
// Open/create files
const file = try std.Io.Dir.cwd().openFile(io, "path.parquet", .{});
defer file.close(io);

// Positional reads (replaces seekTo + read)
const n = try file.readPositionalAll(io, buffer, offset);

// Streaming writer
var buf: [8192]u8 = undefined;
var file_writer = file.writerStreaming(io, &buf);
const writer: *std.Io.Writer = &file_writer.interface;
try writer.writeAll(data);
try file_writer.interface.flush();
```

### ArrayList / ArrayListUnmanaged

```zig
var list: std.ArrayList(T) = .empty;     // NOT .init(allocator), NOT .{}
try list.append(allocator, item);         // allocator passed to ALL methods
const slice = try list.toOwnedSlice(allocator);
list.deinit(allocator);
```

### Memory-backed Writers

```zig
var out: std.Io.Writer.Allocating = .init(allocator);
defer out.deinit();
try out.writer.writeAll(data);
const owned = try out.toOwnedSlice();
```

### stdout / stderr

```zig
var buf: [256]u8 = undefined;
var stdout_writer = std.Io.File.stdout().writerStreaming(io, &buf);
const stdout = &stdout_writer.interface;
try stdout.writeAll("message\n");
try stdout_writer.interface.flush();
```

### Enum Conversion

```zig
// std.meta.intToEnum was removed — use std.enums.fromInt (returns ?T)
const codec = std.enums.fromInt(CompressionCodec, v) orelse return error.InvalidCodec;
```

### Custom Format Functions

```zig
pub fn format(self: @This(), writer: *std.Io.Writer) std.Io.Writer.Error!void {
    try writer.print("{}", .{self.value});
}
```

### JSON Serialization

```zig
// Serialize
var out: std.Io.Writer.Allocating = .init(allocator);
errdefer out.deinit();
try std.json.Stringify.value(data, .{}, &out.writer);
return out.toOwnedSlice();

// Parse
var parsed = try std.json.parseFromSlice(MyData, allocator, json, .{});
defer parsed.deinit();
```

### ArenaAllocator

```zig
_ = arena.reset(.free_all);           // NOT arena.reset()
_ = arena.reset(.retain_capacity);
```

### Build Options (Conditional Compilation)

Compression codecs are controlled via `-Dcodecs=` (default: `all`).

Presets: `all` (C + Zig, Zig used by default), `c-only` (C/C++ only), `zig-only` (no C deps), `none`, or comma-separated list: `c-zstd,zstd,c-snappy,snappy,c-gzip,gzip,c-lz4,lz4,c-brotli,brotli`.

```zig
// Zig implementations (default); C implementations opt-in via c-only or c-<codec>
pub const zig_zstd = if (build_options.enable_zig_zstd) @import("zstd.zig") else {};
pub const zig_snappy = if (build_options.enable_zig_snappy) @import("snappy.zig") else {};
pub const zstd = if (build_options.enable_zstd) @import("c_zstd.zig") else {};
pub const snappy = if (build_options.enable_snappy) @import("c_snappy.zig") else {};
```

In tests, guard codec-specific tests with `supports_*` flags:

```zig
test "my zstd test" {
    if (!build_options.supports_zstd) return;
    // ...
}
```

### WASM Targets

- `export fn` does NOT use `callconv(.C)` on WASM — it won't compile.
- `wasm32-freestanding` won't work with `std.posix`, `std.Thread`, or `std.debug.print`. Use `wasm32-wasi`.

### Before Writing Code

1. Search the codebase for similar patterns first.
2. Compile incrementally — test after every 20-30 lines, not 200.
3. Read compiler errors carefully — Zig's errors are precise.
4. Never call deprecated methods — check for newer alternatives.

## Hardening Requirements

Both reader and writer handle **untrusted data**. Code must return errors instead of panicking on malformed input. See `zig-parquet/HARDENING.md` for full details.

### Never Use `@intCast` on External Data

Use `safe.zig` for all external data casting:

```zig
const safe = @import("safe.zig");

// BAD — panics if value doesn't fit
const size: usize = @intCast(header.page_size);

// GOOD — returns error if value is negative or out of range
const size = try safe.cast(header.page_size);
const count = try safe.castTo(u32, header.num_values);
```

### `catch unreachable` Requirements

When a value is mathematically guaranteed to fit, use `catch unreachable` but MUST include an inline comment explaining why:

```zig
const bit_idx: u3 = safe.castTo(u3, i % 8) catch unreachable; // i % 8 is strictly 0-7

if (value.len > std.math.maxInt(i32)) return error.ValueTooLarge;
const len = safe.castTo(i32, value.len) catch unreachable; // Checked against maxInt(i32) above
```

### Always Bounds-Check Before Slicing or Indexing

```zig
// BAD — panics if out of bounds
const value = data[offset..][0..length];

// GOOD
const value = try safe.slice(data, offset, length);
const item = try safe.get(T, data, index);
```

### Use Checked Arithmetic for External Values

```zig
// BAD — can underflow silently
const values_size = total_size - header_size;

// GOOD
if (total_size < header_size) return error.InvalidSize;
const values_size = total_size - header_size;

// GOOD
const total = std.math.add(usize, a, b) catch return error.Overflow;
```

### Return Context-Aware Errors

Use specific errors (`error.InvalidBitWidth`, `error.EndOfData`, `error.InvalidPageSize`) instead of generic `error.InvalidData`.

### Validate at API Boundaries

```zig
pub fn writeColumn(values: []const T) !void {
    if (values.len > std.math.maxInt(i32)) return error.TooManyValues;
    // ... proceed with encoding
}
```

### Common Safe Casting Helpers

- `safePageSize(i32) -> error{InvalidPageSize}!usize`
- `safeRowCount(i64) -> error{InvalidRowCount}!usize`
- `extractBitWidth([]const u8, usize) -> error{InvalidBitWidth, EndOfData}!u5`
- `safeTypeLength(?i32) -> error{InvalidTypeLength}!usize`

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
